name: histgb_raw_slow_shallow
hypothesis: A depth-3, slow-shrinkage, L2-penalised booster on raw features should behave closer to an additive model and avoid the overfitting that hurt the LightGBM run, potentially edging past the linear baseline.

name: lgbm_raw_tiny_leaves
params: colsample_bytree=0.6, learning_rate=0.02, min_child_samples=60, n_estimators=900, num_leaves=6, reg_lambda=5
hypothesis: The earlier LightGBM failure (0.6448) likely came from too much capacity, so tiny 6-leaf trees, strong L2, column subsampling and balanced weights on raw features should recover the ~0.665 level or better.

name: rf_raw_leaf10
hypothesis: A random forest with min_samples_leaf=10 gives a variance-controlled bagging baseline that reveals whether tree ensembles in general beat the linear model on this dataset.

name: logreg_engineered_C1
hypothesis: Adding engineered ratio/count features to the leading linear model should raise PR-AUC because charge-ratio and add-on counts encode interactions the additive raw encoding cannot express.

name: logreg_raw_baseline
hypothesis: A plain L2 logistic regression on one-hot raw features will set a strong reference PR-AUC (~0.63-0.66) because Telco churn is largely driven by additive contract/tenure/charge effects.

name: histgb_eng_slow_deep_iters
hypothesis: The best-so-far shallow slow booster combined with the engineered ratio/count features and even slower shrinkage with more rounds should extract the same additive signal with less variance and edge past 0.666.

name: logreg_raw_C005
hypothesis: Stronger L2 plus balanced class weights should stabilise the wide one-hot coefficient estimates and improve ranking of the minority churn class over the C=1 unweighted incumbent.

name: logreg_minimal_C3
hypothesis: Since all models cluster at the same PR-AUC, most signal likely sits in seven drivers, and a low-dimensional logreg should match or beat the raw baseline by cutting estimation noise from the wide one-hot design.

name: lgbm_engineered_reg
params: colsample_bytree=0.8, learning_rate=0.05, min_child_samples=40, n_estimators=400, num_leaves=16, reg_lambda=2
hypothesis: A shallow, regularised LightGBM on engineered features should match or beat the linear baseline by capturing tenure/charge-ratio interactions without overfitting the 5.6k training rows.
